steps.intent: France’s primary objective as penholder is to maintain the Council's consensus achieved in resolution 2745 by preserving the targeted sanctions regime exclusively focused on armed groups while fully respecting the CAR Government's sovereign prerogatives. We expect difficult discussions with the Russian Federation and some African members who may advocate for the complete dissolution of the sanctions regime and the termination of the Panel of Experts' mandate. To secure broad support and prevent a veto, the text remains streamlined and focused on curbing illicit weapons flows to non-state armed actors while ensuring unhindered capacity-building for state security forces.

messages.Algeria: Algeria appreciates France's efforts as penholder and fully supports renewing the sanctions regime that rightly targets armed groups while leaving the Central African Republic's national security forces unencumbered. In line with our longstanding position and our work on the Sanctions Committee, we wish to see greater transparency and Committee oversight regarding the tracing and disposal of seized illicit items. We also believe that recognizing the vital contribution of subregional mechanisms, specifically ECCAS and the ICGLR, will further strengthen the draft.
messages.China: China appreciates France's efforts as penholder and welcomes that the draft preserves the landmark decision in resolution 2745 to lift arms embargo restrictions on the Government of the Central African Republic. Sanctions are not an end in themselves and must be kept under constant review with a clear perspective towards further lifting, while respecting the sovereignty and legitimate security needs of the CAR. We also encourage the penholder to ensure the text reflects high standards of impartiality and close consultation between the Panel of Experts and national authorities.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports France's draft resolution extending the targeted arms embargo on armed groups, the sanctions regime, and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We particularly appreciate the continued inclusion of the humanitarian exemption under resolution 2664 (2022) and the focus on curbing illicit trafficking that fuels destabilization. To strengthen the Council's normative framework on protection of civilians, we kindly ask the penholder to incorporate an explicit reference to sexual and gender-based violence and violations against children in PP5.
messages.Greece: Greece fully supports the draft resolution presented by France. The text strikes the right balance by maintaining targeted sanctions against destabilizing armed groups while fully respecting the Central African Republic's sovereign capability to equip its national security forces. We also welcome the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate, whose independent reporting remains essential for Council oversight and regional stability.
messages.Guyana: Guyana expresses appreciation to France for preparing this balanced draft, which rightly preserves the full lifting of restrictions on the Central African Republic’s national security forces while keeping pressure on illegal armed groups. We strongly support the renewal of the targeted measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts to support peace and stability in the CAR. We propose a modest addition to preambular paragraph 4 to underscore the indispensable role of women and youth in advancing inclusive peace and reconciliation.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft resolution circulated by France, which appropriately maintains targeted measures against armed groups while fully respecting the sovereignty of the Central African Republic and upholding the full exemption for state security forces established in resolution 2745 (2024). We appreciate the penholder's balanced approach and support the timely extension of the Panel of Experts and the targeted sanctions regime to assist the Central African Republic in restoring state authority and combating illicit armed groups.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks France for circulating this balanced draft resolution and fully supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We welcome the clear focus on degrading the capacity of armed groups while reaffirming full support for the Central African Republic's authorities, state-building, and security sector reform. We also commend the retention of humanitarian exemptions under resolution 2664 (2022) and the emphasis on the protection of civilians and human rights, and we stand ready to support the adoption of this text.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the draft resolution circulated by France, which effectively maintains targeted sanctions against armed groups while reaffirming that state security forces are not subject to arms embargo measures. We also support the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate, whose reporting is vital for monitoring sanctions compliance and illicit arms flows. We appreciate the penholder's balanced approach and stand ready to support the timely adoption of this resolution.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation welcomes that the draft maintains the complete lifting of restrictions on the legitimate security forces of the Central African Republic achieved last year. It is vital to duly reflect the positive contribution of bilateral partners assisting Bangui at its sovereign request, and to ensure that the Panel of Experts adheres strictly to high evidentiary standards and impartiality without politicizing legitimate security cooperation. We also believe the Council should demonstrate clear readiness to fully adapt and lift remaining sanctions as state authority continues to expand.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks France for circulating this draft, which appropriately maintains the landmark consensus achieved in resolution 2745 (2024) by keeping the arms embargo focused strictly on illicit armed groups while supporting the Central African Republic's state institutions. We suggest explicitly acknowledging the vital contributions of regional and subregional frameworks, particularly ECCAS and the ICGLR, to the peace and stabilization process. We fully support the overall objective of the text and look forward to its consensus adoption.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks France for circulating this timely and balanced draft extending the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We fully support the renewal of the CAR sanctions regime and the Panel's mandate to combat the destabilizing activities of armed groups. In line with our standard priorities on human rights, international humanitarian law, and the protection of civilians, we would welcome the inclusion of explicit references to conflict-related sexual violence, grave violations against children, and accountability.
messages.Somalia: Somalia strongly welcomes that the draft maintains the crucial distinction established in resolution 2745 (2024), ensuring the arms embargo strictly targets illegal armed groups while fully respecting the sovereignty and operational capacity of the Central African Republic's state security forces. We encourage the Council to further acknowledge CAR's progress in weapons and ammunition management and maintain a clear perspective towards the eventual complete lifting of sanctions as stabilization progresses. We stand ready to work constructively with France and Council members to adopt this text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports France's draft resolution to renew the targeted sanctions measures against armed groups and extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts. Maintaining pressure on illicit arms flows and resource trafficking while preserving the Panel's independent reporting is essential for stability in the Central African Republic. We suggest a small addition to preambular paragraph 5 to ensure the Council's condemnation explicitly encompasses conflict-related sexual violence and violations against children.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks France for circulating this balanced draft, which appropriately maintains the targeted sanctions framework against armed groups established in resolution 2745 while ensuring the CAR security forces have the necessary resources. Preserving the mandate of the Panel of Experts is vital for monitoring illicit arms flows, natural resource exploitation, and threats to regional stability. We support the draft as circulated and stand ready to vote in favor.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the French delegation for its constructive engagement and for incorporating our key proposals into revision 1, particularly regarding the reporting and coordination on seized materiel under Committee oversight and the recognition of regional organizations. The draft effectively balances support for the Central African Republic's sovereignty and security forces with targeted measures against armed groups. Algeria fully supports the text and is prepared to vote in favour of its adoption.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder's constructive approach in accommodating our key proposals in revision 1, particularly on reviewing, easing, or lifting measures and ensuring that the Panel of Experts works objectively and in close consultation with the host Government. The draft properly maintains the full exemption for the Central African Republic's national authorities while maintaining targeted pressure on illegal armed groups, fully respecting the country's sovereignty. China supports the draft resolution in its current form and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Denmark: Denmark commends France for its constructive leadership as penholder and welcomes the inclusion of our language on conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and violations against children. The current draft strikes an appropriate balance by maintaining targeted measures against armed groups while supporting the Central African Republic's state institutions and the independent work of the Panel of Experts. Denmark fully supports the draft resolution as presented and looks forward to voting in favour.
messages.Greece: Greece commends France for its stewardship as penholder and fully supports Revision 1 of the draft resolution. The text strikes the right balance by maintaining targeted measures against illicit armed groups while continuing to support the Central African Republic's state institutions and security sector. We also welcome the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate, whose independent monitoring remains indispensable, and we are ready to vote in favour of the text as drafted.
messages.Guyana: Guyana expresses its appreciation to France for accommodating our proposal regarding the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and the engagement of youth in the peace process. We find the revised draft well-balanced, addressing the threat posed by illicit armed groups while fully respecting the sovereignty and security needs of the Central African Republic. Guyana is prepared to support the resolution as currently drafted.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft resolution as currently formulated. We appreciate France's constructive stewardship as penholder in presenting a balanced text that respects the sovereignty of the Central African Republic and upholds the exemption for state security forces. We stand ready to vote in favour of the draft as it goes to the Council.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the penholder. We welcome the continuation of targeted sanctions against armed groups while exempting State security forces, as well as the strong provisions on civilian protection, human rights, and the Panel of Experts' mandate. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text in its current form.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea commends France for presenting a balanced text that appropriately maintains the targeted measures against armed groups while continuing to extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts. The draft respects the sovereignty and operational needs of the Central African Republic's security forces and advances regional stability. We fully support the resolution as drafted and stand ready to vote in favor.
messages.Russian Federation: We thank the French delegation for its constructive approach in incorporating our key proposals into revision 1, particularly regarding the recognition of bilateral assistance in PP3 and the requirements for objectivity and verified sourcing for the Panel of Experts in OP6. To reinforce national ownership and respect for sovereignty, we suggest explicitly noting that any future review or lifting of measures should take into account the views of the Central African authorities in OP9. With this minor addition, the Russian Federation is prepared to support the adoption of the draft resolution.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the French delegation for constructively engaging during consultations and for accommodating our proposal highlighting the vital roles of ECCAS and ICGLR in supporting peace efforts in the Central African Republic. The current text strikes the right balance by maintaining targeted measures against illicit armed groups while fully respecting the CAR's sovereignty and supporting its state security forces. Sierra Leone is ready to support the draft resolution as presented.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks France for its constructive stewardship of this draft and for fully incorporating our proposals on conflict-related sexual violence, violations against children, and accountability. The current text strikes the right balance by maintaining targeted pressure on armed groups, supporting the Panel of Experts, and backing the Central African Republic's peace and stabilization efforts. We fully support the draft resolution in its current form and look forward to its adoption.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the penholder for accommodating our proposals in the revised draft, particularly the recognition of weapons and ammunition management in preambular paragraph 3 and the Council's readiness to ease or lift measures in operational paragraph 9. The current text strikes an appropriate balance that respects the sovereignty and progress of the Central African Republic while maintaining necessary targeted pressure on armed groups. Somalia fully supports the draft resolution and looks forward to voting in favor.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks France for accommodating our proposal in preambular paragraph 5 regarding conflict-related sexual violence and violations and abuses committed against children. We fully support this balanced text, which maintains vital targeted measures against armed groups and preserves the independent monitoring role of the Panel of Experts. We look forward to voting in favour of the resolution.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks France for its balanced stewardship of this draft resolution. The text effectively maintains vital targeted sanctions against armed groups while preserving the Panel of Experts' critical monitoring and reporting mandate, alongside necessary exemptions for Central African Republic security forces. We fully support the adoption of this resolution as drafted.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the targeted arms embargo on armed groups, the targeted sanctions regime, and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic. 

We welcome the constructive spirit shown by Council members throughout the negotiations, and we commend the penholder, France, for its efforts to achieve a consensus text that reflects the Council's unified support for the Central African Republic.

Our vote in favour reaffirms Algeria’s steadfast solidarity with the brotherly Government and people of the Central African Republic in their ongoing efforts to restore peace, enhance security, and extend state authority across the entirety of the national territory. We commend the significant progress achieved by the Central African authorities in advancing security sector reform, disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and repatriation (DDRR), and weapons and ammunition management.

Last year, through resolution 2745 (2024), this Council took a decisive and historic step by lifting the arms embargo on the Government and refocusing the measures exclusively on armed groups. Today’s resolution reinforces this approach, ensuring that national defense and security forces have the necessary means to protect civilians and preserve the nation's sovereignty and territorial integrity, while cutting off the illicit supply of weapons and financing to armed groups that continue to destabilize the country and the wider region.

In our capacity as Chair of the Sanctions Committee, we particularly welcome the provisions encouraging enhanced reporting, transparency, and coordination regarding seized weapons, ammunition, and related materiel. Strengthening the role and oversight of the Committee, in close cooperation with the Central African authorities, remains essential to preventing arms from falling back into the hands of illegal armed groups.

Finally, Algeria reiterates that sanctions are not an end in themselves, but a temporary tool intended to support stabilization and political dialogue. We reaffirm our full support for the implementation of the Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation (APPR-CA) and the Luanda Roadmap, and we urge all international and regional partners to continue providing vital assistance to the Central African Republic on its path toward sustainable peace, institutional consolidation, and socio-economic development.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
(spoke in Chinese): China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted.

Over recent years, the Government of the Central African Republic has actively advanced the peace and political processes, strengthened security sector reform, and made positive progress in expanding State authority and safeguarding national security and stability. China commends the efforts made by the Government of the Central African Republic.

Last year, through resolution 2745 (2024), the Security Council fully lifted the arms embargo measures against the Government of the Central African Republic, marking an important step forward. The resolution just adopted maintains targeted arms embargo measures against armed groups while reaffirming that they do not apply to the Central African Republic security forces. This helps prevent armed groups from acquiring weapons and destabilizing the country, while supporting the Central African Republic in enhancing its national defense and security capabilities.

China has consistently maintained that Security Council sanctions are a means, not an end, and should serve the political settlement of relevant issues. The Security Council should keep the sanctions regime under continuous review in light of developments on the ground and the legitimate concerns of the country concerned, and adjust or lift the relevant measures in a timely manner. We also hope that the Panel of Experts will adhere strictly to its mandate, act in an objective, neutral and transparent manner, base its findings on reliable and verified information, and maintain close communication and cooperation with the Government of the Central African Republic.

China stands ready to work with the international community to continue supporting the Central African Republic in achieving lasting peace, stability, and sustainable development.
after.France:
France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution, which renews for one year the sanctions regime targeting armed groups and associated individuals in the Central African Republic, as well as the mandate of the Panel of Experts.

As penholder, France strove to conduct transparent and inclusive negotiations and took into account the views of all Council members. We thank all delegations for their constructive spirit and engagement, which made it possible to reach a consensus once again this year. We also welcome the close coordination with the Central African authorities throughout this process.

Following the decisive step taken last year with the adoption of resolution 2745 (2024), which fully lifted the arms embargo on the Government of the Central African Republic, today’s resolution maintains the targeted measures strictly directed against armed groups and associated individuals that continue to threaten peace, stability, and the civilian population. The resolution clearly reaffirms that these measures do not apply to the supply of equipment or assistance to the Central African defence and security forces.

By renewing these targeted measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, the Security Council sends a clear and united message: armed groups must cease all hostilities, lay down their weapons, and commit unconditionally to the peace process within the framework of the Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation and the Luanda Roadmap. The illicit trafficking of small arms and light weapons and the illicit exploitation of natural resources, which fuel instability and finance armed groups, must be decisively combated.

France reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic, and will continue to support the Central African people and authorities, alongside MINUSCA and regional and international partners, in their efforts toward sustainable peace, security, and development.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution submitted by France renewing the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic.

We consistently advocate for the Security Council’s sanctions architecture to correspond to the real situation on the ground and to serve the interests of stabilization, rather than hinder the capacity of sovereign States to ensure their own security. In that context, we welcome the fact that the resolution firmly maintains the approach established last year in resolution 2745 (2024), which completely removed the arms embargo on the legitimate Government and national security forces of the Central African Republic, while maintaining targeted restrictions exclusively on illegal armed groups.

The authorities of the Central African Republic, under the leadership of President Faustin-Archange Touadéra, have demonstrated tangible progress in restoring state authority throughout the national territory, implementing security sector reform, and advancing disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and repatriation. These efforts have directly contributed to stabilizing the country and protecting the civilian population from the threat posed by remaining armed formations.

Russia will continue to provide comprehensive support and assistance to the Central African Republic, both bilaterally and within multilateral formats, including through the training and capacity-building of the national armed forces at the request of the official authorities in Bangui.

We also wish to emphasize that the Panel of Experts must conduct its work in strict compliance with its mandate, relying solely on verified, objective and impartial information, and maintaining constructive dialogue and close coordination with the Government of the Central African Republic. Sanctions must remain a flexible tool aimed at supporting peace and political settlement, and we will continue to advocate for their continuous review in light of the evolving realities on the ground.
after.United States of America:
The United States welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime on armed groups in the Central African Republic, as well as the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We thank France for its leadership and efforts as penholder to bring the Council together around this text.

By renewing these targeted measures, the Council reaffirms its commitment to supporting the Central African Republic in addressing the grave challenges posed by illicit arms proliferation, armed group violence, and the destabilizing exploitation of natural resources. As this resolution makes clear, the targeted arms embargo applies exclusively to armed groups and associated actors who continue to perpetrate violence against civilians, peacekeepers, and humanitarian personnel. It in no way restricts the Central African Republic’s legitimate security forces.

We also underscore our steadfast support for the vital work of the Panel of Experts. Objective, independent, and impartial reporting on violations of the sanctions regime, arms trafficking networks, human rights abuses, and the illicit exploitation of natural resources remains indispensable to the work of the Sanctions Committee and the Security Council. We call on all Member States and all relevant actors in the region to cooperate fully and transparently with the Panel, ensuring unhindered access and the safety of its members.

The United States remains committed to supporting the people and the Government of the Central African Republic in their pursuit of lasting peace, security, and stability, including through the implementation of the Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation and the Luanda Roadmap. We will continue to work closely with national authorities, regional partners, and MINUSCA to advance these shared objectives.

Thank you, Mr. President.
